title: [YouPass Collect] - Student room: 2 people & 1 person
prompt: The plans below show a student room for two people and a student room for one person at an Australian university. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The floor plans illustrate the layouts of two types of student accommodation at an Australian university, one designed for two occupants at $350 per week and another for a single resident at $200 weekly.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while both rooms share a similar width of 6 metres, the more expensive option is larger and offers significantly more amenities, including dedicated living and dining areas. In contrast, the cheaper alternative provides only essential facilities for one person.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: The $350 room measures 6 by 4 metres and features a comprehensive layout suitable for two students. In the top left corner sits a bathroom, while the central area is devoted to communal facilities, including a kitchen equipped with a sink, stove, microwave and cupboard, alongside a dining table with chairs. A television and bookshelf are also provided in this shared space. On the right, two beds are arranged perpendicularly, with Bed 1 positioned vertically along the window and Bed 2 placed horizontally below it, each accompanied by an individual study desk.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: By comparison, the $200 room is considerably more compact at 6 by 2.5 metres. The bathroom occupies the left portion of the room, adjacent to a basic kitchen area containing only a sink, stove and microwave, notably without a cupboard. The remaining space on the right houses a single bed and study desk, also benefiting from a window. However, this room lacks the communal amenities found in its more expensive counterpart, such as a television, bookshelf, and dining furniture.
